What is a solution?
questions.a: A uniform mixture where a solute dissolves completely in a solvent - like sugar in water.

questions.q: Name the solute and solvent in sea water.
questions.a: Solvent: water. Solutes: salts (mainly sodium chloride).

questions.q: Why is a solution always clear and stable?
questions.a: Solute particles are too fine to see or settle, and pass through filters.

questions.q: What is a saturated solution?
questions.a: One that holds the most solute it can dissolve at that temperature - extra solute stays undissolved.

questions.q: How can more sugar be dissolved in a saturated sugar solution?
questions.a: Heat it - solubility usually rises with temperature - or add more solvent.

questions.q: What is solubility?
questions.a: The maximum solute that dissolves in 100 g of solvent at a given temperature.

questions.q: Why does warm water hold less dissolved oxygen than cold water?
questions.a: Gases escape faster from warm water - their solubility falls as temperature rises.

questions.q: Why do aquatic animals suffer when pond water gets too warm?
questions.a: Warm water holds little oxygen, so fish and other animals struggle to breathe.

questions.q: How does a fizzy drink lose its fizz when left open in the heat?
questions.a: Carbon dioxide gas escapes faster in warm, open conditions.
